page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2g.16xlarge is a storage-intensive virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical Intel Xeon 8163 processor cores running at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. A key differentiator of this instance is its bundled local storage, which consists of 7679 GB of SSD capacity. Network performance is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate a clear performance profile characterized by moderate multi-threaded capabilities and weaker single-core execution. The single-core performance is rated as weak, with a Geekbench single-core score of 966.0 and a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1108.58. Conversely, multi-threaded operations demonstrate average performance, highlighted by a Geekbench multi-core score of 9986.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 46759.09. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is a notable strength, achieving a strong rating at 199.24 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is average, with uncached large-block reads at 118.82 GB/sec and writes at 47.43 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.i2g.16xlarge offers high resource density, particularly regarding local storage capacity relative to the compute and memory footprint. The inclusion of a massive 7.6 TB local SSD eliminates the need for external block storage attachments for high-throughput local data needs, though users must trade off the lower single-core performance against the high storage density. This instance is best suited for workloads that require substantial local storage capacity and parallel processing capabilities rather than high single-threaded speed. Appropriate workloads include relational and non-relational databases, local data caching, search indexing, and multi-threaded file processing.

Operating on the x86_64 architecture under the KVM hypervisor, this instance delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps. Performance benchmarks show average multi-core capabilities, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 9986.0 and a strong multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 199.24 GB/sec, contrasted by weaker single-core performance. The qualitative value of this instance lies in its high local storage density, making it highly cost-efficient for data-intensive applications that do not require top-tier single-threaded CPU speeds. It is well-suited for database hosting, large-scale file processing, and distributed caching workloads.
